Hospitality Workers Strike Disrupts Hotel and Restaurant Operations Across Qatar

DOHA, June 11 — Thousands of hospitality workers across Qatar began a strike Tuesday, severely impacting operations at hotels, restaurants, and event venues in the Gulf nation, industry officials said.

The walkout, called by the Qatar Hospitality Workers Union (QHWU), is the largest industrial action to hit the sector in years. Union representatives said the strike was triggered by stalled negotiations over wage increases, improved working conditions, and enhanced job security. “We have been in talks for months with management, but our concerns have not been adequately addressed,” said Mansoor Al-Hamad, a spokesperson for the QHWU. “Our members are seeking fair compensation and safer workplaces.”

Major hotel chains, including Desert Pearl Resorts and SunCrest Hospitality, reported significant staff shortages, leading to the closure of several restaurants within their properties and a halt to housekeeping and concierge services. Guests at affected hotels described long wait times for check-in and room service, while some facilities suspended bookings altogether.

Industry group Qatar Hospitality Association estimated that more than 60 percent of frontline staff at international hotels in Doha and Al Wakrah participated in the walkout. The group’s president, Nasser Al-Muftah, called the situation “unprecedented in recent memory,” adding that “all parties need to return to the table urgently for the good of the industry and its workforce.”

Several popular dining venues in Doha’s West Bay district and The Pearl reported closures or limited operating hours, with some management teams stepping in to cover basic functions. “We’re doing our best to keep limited services running with available staff,” said a manager at the Oasis Creek Hotel, who requested anonymity.

Analysts warned that continued disruption could affect the reputation of Qatar’s hospitality sector, particularly with the summer tourism period approaching. “A protracted strike risks long-term damage to client relationships and brand perception,” said hospitality sector analyst Lina Rahman.

Union leaders said the strike would continue until substantive progress is made in negotiations. No date has been set for further talks.
